title: Global methane point sources mapped from EMIT imaging spectroscopy with a vision transformer
summary: MAPL-EMIT used a vision transformer trained on 3.6 million synthetic plumes embedded in EMIT radiance data to map methane sources. Beyond synthetic tests, the paper abstract reports recovery of 84% of known annotated plume complexes across 1,084 EMIT granules. Comparisons with airborne data, landfills and controlled releases supported previously uncaptured sources. This is source-reported validation, not an independent emissions audit.
ai_technology: MAPL-EMIT (end-to-end vision transformer on EMIT hyperspectral radiance)
organization: Google Research; Carnegie Institution for Science; Jet Propulsion Laboratory, California Institute of Technology

evidence.tested: Synthetic tests plus known real plumes, coincident airborne observations, landfill comparisons and controlled-release data.
evidence.unknown: Review scope: complete indexed abstract and metadata; full uncertainty budgets and individual source emissions were not assessed.
evidence.ai_role: An end-to-end vision transformer jointly estimated methane enhancements, plume outlines and source locations from hyperspectral radiance.
